thread:
maya: quick heads-up — I'm bringing up sparkline-3b in dev/stg for an initial sanity pass. Goal: basic correctness + tiny quant check. Can people pick items?

ajay: i'll take tokenization + a serve smoke (sample inputs -> output sanity). planning to run `curl -s -X POST /v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"2+2"}'` against devstg.

maya: thx. baseline prompts i used (tiny probe set): 
- "What is 2+2?"
- "Who is the CEO of Redwood Inference?"
- "Summarize: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog."
- "Translate to French: 'Good morning'"
- "Is a tomato a fruit or a vegetable?"
- "Write a haiku about rain."
Use these for smoke EM/factual checks.

lin: quick note — when i ran int8 locally, i saw punctuation loss on NER-ish outputs. example: input `Who is the CEO of Redwood?` -> `Redwood Inference CEO` (missing name). logs show a few kv-cache warnings: `serving-warning: kvcache-miss 0.026`

ryan: i ran 20 alignment probes from the small harness — fp16 baseline vs sparkline-3b: exact match drop ~3% relative to our in-house 7b baseline. not huge but worth flagging. also a couple hallucinations on the company fact prompt.

smoke-bot: Deploy event: sparkline-3b:v1 deployed to devstg on node gpu-12 at 2065000005 — health checks passed (3/3).

maya: QA items: can someone run arithmetic (2-3) + date reasoning (e.g., "if today is 2026-03-20 what was yesterday's date?") + a short instruction-following prompt (multi-step)? keep replies to 10 examples each. post failures here.

sam: I'll run the quant matrix (fp16 / int8 / int4) over the 200-sample dev harness. quick numbers: fp16 latency ~52ms, int8 ~38ms, int4 ~28ms. accuracy tradeoff: int8 EM down ~4pts vs fp16 on the probe set. uploading CSV to the QA folder.

maya: good — for devstg i propose default to fp16 until we confirm int8 fidelity on the eval suite. we can keep int8 as a perf experiment branch. i'll open a follow-up ticket for systematic quant tests. :thumbsup:

ajay: opened ML-7421 (https://redwood.internal/ticket/ML-7421) — assigned to sam, priority P2. includes checklist: tokenization check, sample outputs, latency/throughput run, small eval harness, throwaway logs.

lin: noted. i'll add a quick eval job to the onboarding harness (runs nightly) and include the 6 probe prompts + the 200-sample quant set. will post results tomorrow morning. :eyes:

maya: awesome, thanks. if anyone sees major hallucination or regression >5% EM drop, flag and we'll rollback to the previous model variant. otherwise we'll keep collecting metrics and reconvene after overnight runs.

sam: posting CSV link: https://redwood.internal/attachments/sparkline-quant-2065.csv — initial summary in comments.

ryan: if helpful i can script a small prompt set that stresses temporal and numeric reasoning and add to harness.

maya: please do. end of quick thread."
